name: SIGMA - DNS Query for a Known Cryptocurrency Mining Pool [cardinality threshold]
description: Elastic threshold companion for rules/sigma/net_zeek_dns_crypto_mining_pool.yml (issue #434, found during #428's security-auditor review). Same gap as net-zeek-dns-doh-non-standard-cardinality.ndjson's own companion (see that file's description for the full reasoning) applied to this rule's operator-domain list instead: the Sigma rule matches on the observed query alone, so any host that can send a DNS packet can emit an arbitrary label under a real mining-pool operator domain (e.g. `dig <random>.nanopool.org` in a loop) and produce a hit with no real mining session ever following. Buckets DNS queries matching the parent rule's own domain list (the exact `sigma convert` output for net_zeek_dns_crypto_mining_pool.yml, kept in sync by hand) by source.ip and alerts when a single source queries >=5 distinct dns.question.name values within the window — a lower bar than the DoH companion's 10, since legitimate traffic to a mining-pool operator domain has essentially no baseline at all (unlike DoH providers, which real browsers/OSes query routinely and sometimes across several documented hostname variants), so less headroom is needed before a repeated-distinct-subdomain pattern here is worth flagging. NOT live-verified end to end (no reachable Elasticsearch/Kibana in the environment this was authored in) — structurally validated only (tests/detections/test_threshold_rules.py: schema, Sigma pairing, lookback-containment math). Tradeoff, recorded per #434's acceptance criteria: still cannot distinguish a real mining session's DNS resolution from a slow/low-volume forged-query campaign staying under the cardinality bar, and a shared NAT/proxy gateway can still collapse multiple real (if unusual) users' queries into one bucket. Response-side qualification (dns.response_code/dns.answers, or zeek.conn/zeek.ssl follow-on correlation, #434's other suggested option) was NOT pursued here for the same reason recorded on the DoH companion — a larger, separately-testable design than this corpus's established cardinality-threshold pattern (auth-win-bruteforce-source-spray.ndjson); left as a distinct follow-up if this volume-shape signal proves insufficient in practice.
query: event.dataset:zeek.dns AND ((dns.question.name:(nanopool.org OR supportxmr.com OR hashvault.pro OR moneroocean.stream OR minexmr.com OR nicehash.com OR f2pool.com OR 2miners.com OR c3pool.com OR herominers.com OR unmineable.com)) OR (dns.question.name:(*.nanopool.org OR *.supportxmr.com OR *.hashvault.pro OR *.moneroocean.stream OR *.minexmr.com OR *.nicehash.com OR *.f2pool.com OR *.2miners.com OR *.c3pool.com OR *.herominers.com OR *.unmineable.com)))
author: Suburban-SOC
false_positives: Deliberate, authorized crypto/security research on an isolated segment repeatedly querying operator subdomains.
A shared NAT/proxy/campus DNS forwarder where multiple distinct real users' queries collapse onto one apparent source.ip.
